credentials.description: API key from the Wave Business portal (sent as Authorization: Bearer); it is tied to a real wallet — Wave documents no sandbox

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Key you generate (UUID v4 suggested, up to 255 characters). Reuse the same key to retry the same request: requests sharing a key never send money more than once.

example_prompt: Add batch Wave payouts to multiple recipients to my payout workflow.

payouts.description: List of payouts to send in a single request.

receive_amount.description: Amount the recipient receives, as a string, without decimals.

payment_reason.description: Reason visible to the recipient (max 40 chars).

id.description: Unique batch identifier (prefix "pb-"). Use it to query GET /v1/payout-batch/{id} until status is 'complete'.

details.description: Validation details returned on request-validation-error. Each entry contains loc (field location), msg (message), type (error type). Can be null or absent (measured on 2026-10-24 on 401 errors) — check before iterating.

gotchas: Every POST /v1/payout-batch request must include a unique Idempotency-Key header (UUID v4 recommended, max 255 chars). A batch can distribute funds to dozens of recipients — a retry without an idempotency key can trigger every payout twice.
This endpoint is asynchronous — it immediately returns a batch.id without waiting for the payouts to be processed. Poll GET /v1/payout-batch/{id} until status === 'complete'.
batch.status === 'complete' does not mean that all payouts succeeded. Inspect the status of each individual payout in the response — some can be 'failed' while others are 'succeeded'.
There is no 'success' or 'failed' status at the batch level itself, only 'processing' and 'complete'. The actual result is in each payout.
Each payout in the batch is processed independently. A failure on one payout (e.g. insufficient-funds) does not cancel the others.

If the API key was created with request signing (optional Business Portal setting), every call must carry Wave-Signature: t={timestamp},v1={HMAC-SHA256(timestamp + raw body)} computed with the signing secret (format wave_sn_AKS_…, shown only once) — empty body for a GET. Without it: 401 missing-signature; other codes: invalid-signature, invalid-signature-format, invalid-signature-timestamp, expired-signature-timestamp (timestamp more than 5 minutes in the past or more than 30 seconds in the future). The setting is permanent for a key: to drop it, revoke the key and create another one.

[MUST TELL USER] The API IP whitelist turns on as soon as the first address is added in the Business Portal (Developer section) and can no longer be turned off from the portal — you have to go through your Wave account manager. Calls from an unlisted IP get 403 ip-not-allowed: on hosting without a fixed outbound IP (serverless functions, most PaaS), do not add any IP before you have a fixed egress.
